actual.title: Who really reads
actual.summary: Who really reads: {{seen}} seen, {{silent}} silent, {{notRegistered}} not registered
actual.help: What the platforms said at the last read in {{environment}}: Snowflake users and roles from ACCESS_HISTORY (metadata only, no query text) and Kafka consumer groups with offsets on the port’s topics – beside the registered consumers.
actual.hiddenPlatform: A platform you may not see
actual.hiddenConsumer: A consumer you may not see

read.notAvailable: {{platform}}: ACCESS_HISTORY is not available (an edition without it, or a role that may not read it) – who reads is not known there.
read.noObjects: {{platform}}: nothing bound here that the platform reports reads of.

actual.declaredTitle: Registered consumers of {{name}} and whether they read
actual.identitiesHelp: How the consumer reads: user:NAME (a Snowflake user), role:NAME (a Snowflake role), group:NAME (a Kafka consumer group). A registered user is also matched by their user name and e-mail address.
actual.identitiesInvalid: Not an identity: {{list}} – use user:, role: or group:
actual.registerHint: Register these consumers on the port, or name their identities on an existing registration, so that they are known.

requests.title: Access requests
requests.pageHelp: Requests for access to output ports of data products: what waits for your decision, what you asked for, and everything you may see. An approved request registers the consumer; the platform team grants the access.
requests.productHelp: People ask for access to an output port with the purpose and until when; the product owners decide (two people when the product is rated high or above). An approval registers the consumer and, where the settings below say so, records the ticket and starts the platform team’s process.
requests.help: The product owners decide. Steward does not grant on the platform itself: an approval registers the consumer, and the platform team grants the access.
requests.agreementInvalid: The address must start with http:// or https://
requests.approveHint: Approving registers the consumer and is recorded as an access change. You confirm it is you first.
requests.approveFirstHint: The product is rated high or above: a second person approves after you.
requests.processHint: The process “{{name}}” starts with the request as its inputs.
requests.ticketHelp: The number of the platform team’s ticket – it is recorded as a ticket reference of the product.
requests.reasonRequired: Give the reason for the refusal

empty.mine: You have not asked for access yet – open a data product’s port to ask.
empty.all: No access requests of data products you may see.

requests.sent: Request sent – you can follow it under Data → Access requests
requests.approvedFirst: First approval recorded – a second person decides
requests.withdrawConfirm: Withdraw your request for {{port}}? It cannot be sent again – ask anew if you need access later.
requests.emptyStatus: No request of this status – clear the status to see all.

reviews.title: Port access reviews
reviews.help: Who consumes an output port, reviewed periodically: the registrations, who really reads and – from an access check – the grants on the port’s objects are frozen into the review; you keep or remove each, a second person approves, the review is sealed. Registrations decided “remove” end when it is approved.
reviews.checkHelp: Its grants on the port’s objects are reviewed too – read now, else its latest snapshot.
reviews.checkLive: Grants read now from the access check “{{name}}” ({{date}}).
reviews.checkSnapshot: Grants from the latest snapshot of “{{name}}” ({{date}}) – the live read failed.
reviews.verifyBad: The seal does not match – the review was changed in the database.
reviews.openNamed: Open the access review of {{port}} in {{environment}}

settings.title: Access settings
settings.processHelp: A process the platform team owns, started live as the approver with the request as inputs (dataProduct, port, environment, consumer, identities, until, purpose, requestId). Its own approvals apply.
settings.hiddenProcess: a process you may not see
settings.ticketSourceHelp: The approver may give the ticket of the grant; it is recorded as a ticket reference of this source.
settings.reviewMonthsHelp: A port access review is due this many months after the last approved one (empty: no periodic review).
settings.help: Who manages the product changes these settings.

promotion.title: Promote {{name}}
promotion.help: Proposes the members and port bindings of the next environment from the current one by the environment rules of the discovery sources (DEV_DB.SALES.ORDERS → PROD_DB.SALES.ORDERS; the same name for platforms per environment). Steward deploys nothing: the promotion is recorded with its evidence.
promotion.oneEnvironment: The product has one environment – add the next one first (Overview → Environments).
promotion.noRules: No environment rules on these platforms: the same names are looked for.
promotion.hidden_one: {{count}} element found there that you may not see is left out.
promotion.hidden_other: {{count}} elements found there that you may not see are left out.
promotion.targetBound: bound there already (the elements found are added)
promotion.hiddenContract: a contract you may not see
promotion.empty: The product has nothing in {{environment}} to promote.
promotion.evidenceHelp: The change record, ticket or process run that approved the promotion.
promotion.done: Promoted – the members and bindings are added; what is missing stays listed.

endorsement.title: Endorsement

reviews.expired: Expired on {{date}} – it no longer counts for maturity level 5.
reviews.breakingChange: A bound data contract had a breaking change: endorse it again after a review.
reviews.belowFloor: The rating is below its data objects without a reason: endorse it again after a review.

endorsement.none: Not endorsed. The owners of its domain endorse a product they trust; maturity level 5 counts a valid endorsement on top of level 4.
endorsement.endorsers: Who may endorse it: the owners of its domain – {{list}}.
endorsement.managers: Its domain has no owners: the module’s managers endorse it.
endorsement.ownProduct: Nobody endorses a product they own.
endorsement.formHelp: An endorsement says the product can be relied on. It is valid until the review date (at most 12 months) and needs a review after a breaking change of a bound contract or a rating below the floor.

ropa.title: Records of processing
ropa.help: Data objects with personal data and where they are processed (GDPR Art. 30): products, purposes, legal basis, categories, recipients, retention and the platforms with their suppliers.
ropa.disclaimer: A working view for the data protection officer from the data products – not the record of processing activities itself. What you may not see is counted, never named.
ropa.empty: No data objects with personal data that you may see.
ropa.hiddenDomain: a domain you may not see
ropa.csvNamed: Download the records of processing as CSV
ropa.pdfNamed: Download the records of processing as PDF
